author: Murray
comment:
You have the answers to the background music already; unless we can find some open source, i.e. no copyright, tracks we can't use it unfortunately.

As for sustainability, as long as we have a web connection we're fine for blogging and uploading photographs. Vlogging is reserved for free web connections where we're staying for a while; the actual video can be shot and edited without internet and we can store it until we find somewhere to upload it but it is the most intensive so it's use will be limited.

I think the main black hole will be in Malaysia. We can find internet connections relatively cheaply (if Borneo is anything to go by) however WiFi zones are somewhat harder to find.

Twitter thoughts of course help when we don't have any web connection. Hopefully though, providing we have something worth blogging about, the process will be sustainable.

author: MumJo
comment:
Thanks for this lovely tribute to Grandpa, Mike. I'll email you with a little more detail but the funeral was lovely and you were there in suit (on Daniel!) and spirit if not in person.

What are you up to during your last five days in Oz? The Cairns beaches look very uninviting! Did you scuba or snorkel on the reef?

author: Adrian
comment:
Mike - a lovely and moving tribute to your Grandpa. You clearly have some lovely memories to treasure.

Hope the foot has healed properly. Enjoy your last two days in Oz.

author: Mike
comment: read the next blog for what I did :) also final pics up of Oz!

author: MumJo
comment: I presume, since you are still able to write , that the tarantula-like spider wasn't one! Your feet seem to be suffering, Mike. Glad the reef was good. How are you going to fill the time in in Cairns? It doesn't sound to be unduly exciting.

author: MumJo
comment: Just love your final description of Oz, Murray. You have been exceptionally unlucky weather-wise but still seem to have got a lot from the experience. Malaysia can only be drier - or is it the wet season?!

author: Adrian
comment:
Singapore seems to be a wonderful mixture of cultures. Yet another of your destinations that I have not been to and your description makes it very inviting. The pictures show lots of interesting architecture existing alongside old colonial and some very eastern buildings - all fascinating. Have you mostly stuck to the business centre, do you think? Could that be why there are so few people in the streets?

Singapore noodles are a favourite of mine - good to hear that you have tried the real thing! Hope Kuala Lumpar is as good an experience.

author: MumJo
comment: Both in photos and blogs, Mike gives the wider perspective, as in the enclosures at the zoo and Murray zooms in on the detail. Great teamwork even if unintentional! Mike I think you might be getting into both writing and photography more - you are doing both well. Not quite to Murray's standards but very creditable!

author: MumJo
comment: You lads really compliment each other in the way you write - Mike gives the overview and Murray the detail. It's brilliant. Just loved today's offerings - keep it up boys!

author: Adrian
comment: What a fabuous looking zoo. A pity to hear that the big cats are still confined to small spaces. Some of Mike's pictures show almost natural habitats with no sense that they are in enclosures. You were clearly in your element, Murray.

author: Murray
comment: Just to let people know only a third of my photos uploaded, they shouldnt have even been on the blog yet :P The rest are coming shortly :)

author: Adrian
comment: Oh, dear! Think you were lucky - what time was the train to leave?! Also, crowded trains can be dodgy for backpackers. I remember an incident on a jam-packed Paris Metro when I couldn't turn around to protect my pack from exploring hands! I am sure you will be better prepared next time. Super pics, Murray.

author: Murray
comment: Oh the train was the lap of luxury, we had seats to ourselves and even a TV that we couldnt hear at all at the front of our carriage :P It was just getting to the train and working out when everyone suddenly left at one stop that we had to get out to go through customs again as well xD Still not sure if we're legally allowed to be in Malaysia, flying out to Borneo is going to be interesting...o_O

author: MumJo
comment: Good to hear a bit about the stays in Sydney and Newcastle, Mike. Sounds like Australia has had plenty rain! We have too and I think the Adcocks will have found Skye very wet and windy (best way to see it?!). Are you now adept surfers? What next? Enjoy Brisbane and beyond.

author: MumJo
comment: Great to get all the Kuala Lumpur detail. You are not so much lazy as worn out by all the walking by the sounds of it! I guess Borneo is just as humid but hopefully fascinating. Weather here is a bit odd - we had a tropical storm on Monday with flash flooding and some damage (not at home, it bypassed Low Row and hayton I think) although wind blew our gate down (again!)

author: Adrian
comment:
Good to catch up on the Kuala Lumpar experience. Always knew Murray couldn't get out of bed in the morning - but thought the free 'cultural' breakfast would have done the trick. Shows some things don't change! Thanks for the blog, glad you enjoyed the escalators - simple pleasures, eh? Mind you, I completely get the need to stay in the air conditioning.

We hadn't realised how much of Kuala Lumpar you had done before, Mike. I am sure that Murray enjoyed you showing him around.

author: Adrian
comment: Fantastic description of your feelings about returning to Borneo, Murray. We lived it with you all over again. It seems you were lucky in the Park, however your previously gained knowledge obviously helped you out. We know, only too well, from our experiences in Eqypt that ATMs (and in our case even the banks) are not always reliable when trying to withdraw or change money. A good travel lesson learnt, I think.

author: Adrian
comment:
We have had a good look at both sets of pictures now and are very impressed. It seems the weather has been good to you - is it as hot as Kuala Lumpar? We thought the building in Mike's pictures was familiar, amazing that you went back to the same hostel as before. The locals are clearly not too bothered about the shower room falling down. Bet you had quick showers! Steve says that rugby (SA v Lions) just about to kick off (means his mind is elsewhere) - says goodbye and enjoy last days in KK. Perhaps the TAR islands look inviting now?

Rodgers, Kennellys, Blows and Bothma are all gathering in Noordhoek to watch the rugby - I am going shopping!

author: MumJo
comment:
At the Low Row end its the Grand Prix qualifiers occupying Doug! Last at Silverstone - should have got tickets. I am off to cook.

Great to hear and see all the impressions/insects of Borneo! Where are you going now?

author: Murray
comment: Perhaps a day at TAR tomorrow, hopefully still on the cards, as for the weather it is as hot but actually sunny and not as much humidity so its a lot more pleasant a heat. :)

author: MumJo
comment: Thought provoking ruminations on revisiting! Yeah, get Mike to write the newcomers blog.

author: Adrian
comment:
Can see how going back without the group dynamic would have made this a different experience. Also, perhaps less pre-planning? Your experiences in Oz and NZ would also have been improved by the whole 'backpacker bus route' thing - you haven't had that in Malaysia. That said, I think it has been an achievement. You have had to decide and deal with problems as they cropped up - on your own, including all the travel arrangements.

Hope the trip back to Singapore goes smoothly. Will it be back to the same hostel there?

author: Adrian
comment: Great blog, Mike. Hope you enjoyed Borneo - despite the various woes. Steve and I both remember similar experiences with backpack travel, good to see that you have experienced the real, unsanitised thing. Loved your descriptions, we hooted with laughter at the more awful and odorous encounters. You livened up our day! Although, Steve was already on a high after the Lions victory. No doubt you will have to cope with Grandpa Rodger's disappointment!

author: MumJo
comment: Yeah - you used my title idea!! I thought it was inspired. Glad to hear about your Borneo observations and to hear from Twitter that SA is going well. Which big four did you see? Must go, going out for Thai banquet with Adcocks and Shona late as regatta on at Talkin Tarn so lots of ice-cream for her to serve. See you in two weeks today. Maybe Greece with Craibs?!

author: MumJo
comment: Thank you, Mike. You made me laugh and cry! Love the sentiments. Not saying publicly how old I am but getting closer to 100 every year. Enjoy the last week both of you. We will be at Manchester to meet you on Saturday and can't wait to hear anything we haven't already hear and to be feeding you abd washing your boxers again!

author: Sho
comment: YOU JOBBY!

author: Mike
comment: shhhhhhh you chump

author: MumJo
comment: Great last blog, Mike. You've certainly seen lots of animals even if you are sick of them now - a natural naturalist not! Not very reassured about the bungy jumping but glad you are in one piece for now. See you on Saturday. XX

author: Adrian
comment: [Steve] Well said Murray; and also thanks from us here to Alex and Val for looking after them so well and for organising and undertaking such a wonderful end-of-tour road trip for the lads. Three cheers. Love from Steve.

author: MumJo
comment: Great to see you both at Manchester Airport around midday - 9 hours ago! Wonderful to have Mike fill us in on much detail en route to a less snowy (it was considerably more than one millimetre, Murray) but torrentially wet Cumbria and Low Row after a bit of a detour due to the A69 being closed! Nice to get the two fresh blogs this evening bringing the world trip full circle. We are really going to miss our twice daily fixes. Thanks to all who made this possible for the lads.

author: Adrian
comment:
Last couple of blogs - it does feel like the end of a good novel and we are just waiting for the illustrations (photos) to catch up.

You have both done so well in keeping your family and friends informed of your experiences, it has been a real treat and made us feel as though we were with you and not so far away.

This has been 6 months of adventure, challenges and successes that you can both look back on in future years. Keeping to your itinerary; not losing anything on the way (or losing your way!); making good friends and broadening your horisons - all in no small measure due to the way you have conducted yourselves. A real achievement for both of you. Well done!

author: MumJo
comment:
Brill! For someone who doesn't like writing, Mike, you've done a great job throughout, as of course has your partner in crime, Murray. In case any readers don't get the Sanna Bay bit - it is in Scotland on the Ardnamurchan Peninsula - the most westerly point on the British Isles. It is beautiful if you get the weather - nothing there but white beaches, some cottages, a few people and sea, sea, sea. Mike is now taking his spade to Greece for some castle building R & R - as if he needs it!

Thanks too from Doug and I to everyone who contributed in any way to this amazing trip.

author: Adrian
comment:
What a wonderful final round up of the last six months, Mike. I still have to see Sanna Bay, - but am sufficiently inspired by your trip to want to see some of the places you travelled to since February.

While thanks are the order of the day - we (The Adcocks) are very conscious of all the kindness that was extended to the boys during their travels and which helped to ease them through all the different countries and experiences. It certainly helped the parents 'ease of mind' as well. Thank you all.
